title: ReCompress: Query-Aware Rewriting and Tiered Memory for Efficient LLM Context Compression
abstract: Large language models face two compounding token inefficiencies: single-turn contexts containirrelevant passages that consume budget without contributing to answers, and multi-turn conversationsresend full history every call, causing cumulative cost to grow quadratically with conversation length.Deletion-based compression approaches are query-independent and cannot drop entire irrelevantpassages; multi-turn memory systems lack explicit protection for the bridging facts that multi-hopreasoning depends on. We present ReCompress, a two-component system addressing both regimes. Aquery-aware rewriting compressor, distilled into a 1.5B student (Qwen2.5-1.5B + LoRA), outperformsbear-1.1 by +0.252 F1 on HotpotQA while emitting roughly 8.5× fewer tokens (48 vs. 409 at a ratio-0.3 compression instruction). The gain is significant on multi-hop question answering with distractors(HotpotQA, and the near-in-distribution 2WikiMultiHop, +0.180 F1) and positive-but-not-significanton more dissimilar tasks (MuSiQue, SQuAD) at n = 50; we make the narrower claim the datasupports. We further audit the result against ourselves: the gap survives an independent solver, and amask-the-answer probe shows a substantial share of the margin comes from reliably retaining theanswer-bearing span at a 3.5% budget where deletion truncates it. A tiered multi-turn framework,RbD-Compress, holds the context sent to the solver flat through protected trauma memory, aversioned checkpoint stack with rollback, and Echidna, an intelligent trigger that reads traumamemory before compression decisions, at no measurable loss in answer quality — a flatness resultwe scope carefully against per-turn compression overhead and KV-caching assumptions. Our resultsshow that query-aware rewriting and deletion-based compression serve complementary operatingregimes.

title: Epistemic Entropy Fields: A Geometric Theory of Hallucination in Language Models
abstract: Language models generate fluent falsehoods because they lack a principled representation of their own uncertainty about facts. Existing approaches treat hallucination as a statistical or engineering problem; none frames it as a geometric property of the model's latent space. We introduce Epistemic Entropy Fields (EEF), a differential-geometric theory that treats an LLM's latent manifold as a Riemannian space equipped with an evidence-conditioned metric. The framework derives epistemic geodesics for uncertainty-aware generation, introduces a directional stress tensor for uncertainty that varies across semantic dimensions, and formulates the hallucination invariant as a geometric calibration condition. Three implementation strategies are derived, with inference overheads from 1.05x to 1.36x. A training-time strategy requires no architectural modification and adds zero inference cost. Proof-of-concept experiments on GPT-2 (124M parameters) show that geometric and linguistic objectives can coexist: a refined training configuration achieves validation loss 0.0175 versus a baseline of 0.0160, with the geodesic loss decreasing 89% during training. A synthetic-label detector achieves 90% accuracy. These results establish mechanical viability, not practical efficacy. Benchmark evaluation on TruthfulQA, HaluEval, and comparison with F-DPO is ongoing. The primary contribution is theoretical: a geometric vocabulary for characterising model uncertainty, with empirical feasibility as a prerequisite step.

title: Generative Robust Optimisation
abstract: Classical uncertainty sets for robust optimisation impose fixed geometric shapes that cannot represent the complex dependencies present in real-world data. We propose Generative Robust Optimisation (GRO), a framework in which a deep generative model defines the uncertainty set as the image of a neural network decoder over a calibrated latent set, naturally accommodating nonlinear correlations, asymmetry, and multimodality. A five-point evaluation framework (reconstruction fidelity, distribution matching, latent regularity, robust relevance, and computational tractability) provides systematic, model-agnostic criteria for assessing any neural network-based uncertainty set. We instantiate this framework with a Wasserstein Adversarial Autoencoder employing Gaussian mixture model-guided training for latent regularity and constraint-consistency regularisation for robust relevance. Restricting the decoder to ReLU activations enables exact worst-case verification through mixed-integer programming embedding. Extensive experiments on a production planning problem across six uncertainty distributions and six generative architectures, together with a multi-period facility location study, validate the framework and demonstrate that systematic attention to all five criteria yields uncertainty sets that are simultaneously expressive, well-calibrated, and optimisation-tractable.

title: Specificity- and Calibration-Aware Breast Ultrasound Segmentation via Entropy-Guided Boundary Supervision
abstract: Lesion segmentation in breast ultrasound involves two related challenges. In images with lesions, speckle noise, low tissue contrast, and posterior acoustic shadowing cause boundary leakage and incomplete contour delineation. In images without lesions, those same artifacts generate false-positive activations in regions resembling solid lesion tissue. This study addresses both failure modes through a single modification to the training objective. Rather than weighting every boundary pixel equally, the proposed loss scales contour penalties by per-pixel predictive entropy and the ground-truth boundary map, concentrating gradient emphasis on lesion margin locations where the network remains uncertain. The loss was evaluated on the BUSI dataset through a controlled ablation against two baselines: a model without boundary supervision and a model with uniformly weighted boundary binary cross-entropy. Across 97 lesion-containing test images, mean Dice scores were statistically indistinguishable between the proposed method and the no-boundary baseline (0.7624 versus 0.7616, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.27), confirming that lesion segmentation quality is preserved. The primary effect appears in specificity. False-positive activations on 20 no-lesion test images fell from 14 of 20 and 19 of 20 for the two baselines to 5 of 20 with the proposed approach (McNemar p = 0.012 and 0.0005). Non-overlapping Wilson 95% confidence intervals confirm the difference is both statistically significant and practically substantial. A post-hoc spatial temperature scaling step further reduced expected calibration error from 0.0201 to 0.0095 without altering segmentation masks. Entropy-guided boundary supervision and spatial calibration thus function as complementary training-level and inference-level refinements that improve specificity and probability reliability within a U-Net framework.

title: The Algorithmic Product Leader (Masterclass)
abstract: The Algorithmic Product Leader is an executive presentation examining how artificial intelligence is reshaping product management. Originally prepared for and presented to a private corporation in Uppsala, Sweden, it explores the transition from conventional software products, built around largely deterministic behaviour, to AI-enabled systems whose outputs require continuous evaluation, monitoring, guardrails and fallback mechanisms. The presentation considers the implications of this shift across seven dimensions: speed, competitive advantage, unit economics, human capital, product lifecycles, governance and trust. It also introduces practical frameworks for distinguishing what organisations should automate, where AI should augment human capabilities and which areas of judgment should remain firmly protected. Designed as a strategic masterclass and discussion framework, the presentation argues that AI does not eliminate product leadership: it raises the importance of judgment, accountability and deliberate product design.

title: A Post-Quantum Secure Lattice-Based Forward-Secure Identity Based Encryption with Applications to Internet of Things Architecture
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to an unprecedented scale of data exchange across heterogeneous and resource-constrained devices. Ensuring confidentiality and secure key management in such environments is challenging. Traditional public-key infrastructures require heavy certificate-handling overhead. Identity-Based Encryption (IBE) offers a lightweight alternative by deriving public keys directly from device identities, making it attractive for IoT deployments. However, IoT devices are highly vulnerable to side-channel and key-extraction attacks, motivating the need for Forward-Secure IBE(FS-IBE), where the compromise of a current secret key does not threaten past communications. Existing FS-IBE constructions based on classical hardness assumptions are not secure in the era of post-quantum, while the lattice-based (LWE-based) forward-secure scheme suffer from large key and ciphertext sizes, limiting their suitability for constrained IoT systems. Here, we propose a new lattice-based fs-IBE scheme in the ring setting, relying on the RLWE assumption to achieve post-quantum security and significant efficiency gains. Our design uses trapdoor delegation with a minimal-cover mechanism over a binary tree. It results in compact public parameters and efficient per-epoch key updates. Compared to prior LWE-based constructions, our scheme reduces public key, secret key, and ciphertext sizes, and thus, making it better suited for practical IoT environments.

title: Enhancing Protein Representation Learning via Manifold Restore Mixing
abstract: Data augmentation (DA) has been proven to be an effective means for improving protein representation learning (PRL) by generating additional training samples. Although mainstream perturbation- and sampling-based augmentation methods can produce data containing sufficient variations, they carry the risk of disrupting the protein structure and function. Some crafted protein homology modeling tools can generate conformations, but reduce structural diversity. The above dilemmas lead us to a question: Can we restore the disrupted structure caused by DA operations, providing data with both the original structure and diverse variations? In this work, we first analyze and empirically reveal the structure defect and performance degradation issues of existing DA methods. Based on the findings, we propose a simple yet effective DA method, Manifold Restore Mixing (MRM), for protein representation learning. Specifically, inspired by manifold mixup, we mix the hidden representations of original and augmented protein data to generate new samples that restore structural information lost in DA while introducing diverse variations. Furthermore, we develop a sample difficulty scheduler that adjusts the beta distribution in mixup to provide models with progressively challenging mixed samples during training, which improves the final performance. Comprehensive experiments on various PRL backbones and downstream tasks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization of our method. The complete code and weights will be released upon acceptance. We provide a implementation at https://github.com/KingGugu/MRM.

Comprehensive experiments on various PRL backbones and downstream tasks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization of our method. The complete code and weights will be released upon acceptance. We provide a implementation at https://github.com/KingGugu/MRM.

title: FIDELITY LANDSCAPE PATTERN ANALYSIS FOR PHASE STABILITY ASSESSMENT IN QUANTUM STATE VERIFICATION
abstract: Phase stability verification is a critical requirement for the reliable operation of modular quantum architectures.In Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices, stochastic phase drift pro-gressively degrades computational fidelity and makes efficient diagnostic methods a practical necessity.This paper introduces a task-specific framework for assess-ing phase consistency using a Fidelity Pattern Corre-lation (FPC) algorithm.By analyzing the structural recurrence of fidelity landscapes generated through parameterized phase sweeps, we define a persistence metric Γ that quantifies temporal phase coherence across repeated experimental executions.Numerical simulations demonstrate that stable phase manifolds exhibit high structural correlation (Γ ≈ 0.95), while stochastic drift produces measurable structural frag-mentation.The proposed approach offers a polyno-mially scalable classical post-processing method that serves as a practical alternative to full quantum state reconstruction for phase stability assessment in two-qubit modular settings.

title: The Platform Proprietor Non-Appropriation Doctrine A Source-Fidelity Governance Analysis of AI Platforms, Competitor Data, User-Created Intellectual Property, and Market Intelligence Risk
abstract: This paper explains a major governance problem with AI platforms: the company that provides the tool may also be building products that compete with the people using that tool. In simple terms, if a creator, researcher, inventor, developer, or small business uses an AI product to build something original, the AI company should not be able to claim ownership over that work just because its platform helped process, edit, organize, or generate parts of it. That would be like Microsoft claiming it owns every document created on a Windows computer, Apple claiming it owns every photo taken on an iPhone, or Adobe claiming it owns every design made in Photoshop. The toolmaker owns the tool, but the creator owns the work. The paper argues that AI platforms create a special risk because they do more than store files. They can read, analyze, summarize, classify, improve, and transform user ideas. That means a user may accidentally reveal business plans, inventions, source code, research frameworks, product designs, legal strategies, or other valuable intellectual property to a company that may also be a competitor. The issue is not only whether user data is used for model training. Even if a company says it does not train on certain customer data, the company could still potentially gain value from user materials through product ideas, feature development, market intelligence, safety frameworks, business strategy, or investor-facing language. This creates a source-fidelity problem: the original source of the idea must remain attached to the creator, not absorbed into the platform. The paper proposes a rule called the Platform Proprietor Non-Appropriation Doctrine. This means an AI platform provider should not convert user access, prompts, files, feedback, drafts, or outputs into ownership, product strategy, market advantage, or competing commercial systems without clear permission, attribution, or licensing. The paper calls for stronger protections, including audit logs, competitor-data firewalls, clear limits on how user content can be used, stronger separation between customer content and internal product teams, and public disclosures when AI companies move toward public markets. The core message is simple: using an AI tool should not mean surrendering your ideas. The platform may provide the instrument, but the creator remains the source.

title: Al-ʻAranjiyya: An Expert-Annotated Corpus of Covert Linguistic Hybridization in Modern Arabic News Text
abstract: Al-ʻAranjiyya is the first publicly released, expert-annotated corpus of covert linguistic hybridization (al-ʻaranjiyya, العَرَنْجِيَّة): the covert adoption of foreign structural and semantic patterns into Arabic prose that, unlike code-switching, leaves no surface marker and requires structural and semantic reasoning to detect. It comprises 1,000 Modern Standard Arabic news articles (78,601 running words) sampled from the publicly available SANAD dataset and balanced across six domains (Culture, Finance, Medical, Politics, Sports, Technology), annotated by two professional Arabic linguists into 6,093 spans and 7,881 label assignments across six categories (Syntactic Template, Stylistic Template, Semantic Template, Lexical Error, Lexical Borrowing, Morphological Error) with substantial inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.67); each span carries character offsets, one or more labels, and a free-text rationale.

title: Sampling as Reasoning, Reasoning as Sampling: Structural Parallels and Their Limits Across Generative Inference and Chain-of-Thought
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models and sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference in probabilistic graphical models share a common mathematical skeleton: both decompose a joint distribution as a product of conditional distributions over sequential steps. This paper consolidates that structural parallel and examines where it yields actionable insights and where it breaks down. We draw on recent preprints to establish four grounded observations. First, the autoregressive product-of-conditionals formulation of CoT reasoning is formally analogous to the sequential factorization used in SMC, though the primary sources do not derive principled resampling or degeneracy diagnostics from this analogy. Second, antithetic sampling demonstrably reduces variance and improves diversity in diffusion model outputs; whether an analogous construction for reasoning traces would reduce answer variance remains speculative. Third, sample-consistency hallucination detectors such as SelfCheckGPT measure inter-sample disagreement as a proxy for hallucination risk, bearing surface resemblance to SMC variance diagnostics, but the sources do not characterize them as such. Fourth, faithfulness failures in CoT involve distinct causal and coverage dimensions that formal verification does not resolve. Throughout, we carefully distinguish what the cited sources establish from what remains conjecture, offering a hedged map of where sampling theory may—and may not—illuminate language model reasoning. title: Hierarchical Quantum Logical Processor with Amortized Long-Range Connectivity
abstract: High qubit overhead is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes offer high encoding efficiency but typically require non-local connectivity in every syndrome extraction cycle, incurring additional physical errors and implementation complexity. We introduce a hierarchical logical processor (HLP) architecture that implements a high-rate quantum CSS code with distance-$d_{0}$ rotated surface codes (RSC), allowing long-range connectivity to be used only once every $Θ(d_{0})$ rounds of surface-code syndrome extraction. HLPs introduce elongated RSC patches called shuttle buses. Using transversal hybrid-unit CNOT gates, a single shuttle bus can simultaneously couple to multiple standard RSC patches. This capability enables efficient level-1 syndrome extraction with suppressed level-1 error correlations and supports highly parallel logical Pauli measurements. We perform circuit-level simulations of several concrete HLP constructions and benchmark both logical memory and logical Pauli measurement performance. At a physical error rate of $10^{-3}$, a hierarchical logical processor can achieve 3-4 times higher qubit efficiency than the rotated surface code and 20-30 times shorter logical error-correction cycle times than the yoked surface code.

title: Projection-Volume Fidelity Divergence: Diagnosing and Controlling Optimization Drift in Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Tomography
abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography is a severely ill-posed inverse problem, where recent 3D Gaussian Splatting methods offer an efficient explicit representation for tomographic reconstruction. However, we find that projection-domain optimization can be misleading in this setting: the rendered projections may continue to improve while the reconstructed volume deteriorates. We identify this failure mode as Projection-Volume Fidelity Divergence (PVFD), a representation-level optimization drift caused by anisotropic Gaussian deformation and view-specific primitive co-adaptation under sparse Radon constraints. To characterize this behavior, we introduce geometry- and volume-level diagnostics that measure needle-like Gaussian degeneration and the stability of the voxelized density field. Based on these observations, we propose LADES, a ground-truth-free optimization controller for sparse-view Gaussian tomography. LADES combines Linearly Annealed Dropout, which applies strong stochastic masking in early training to disrupt premature primitive co-adaptation and gradually restores full capacity for structural consolidation, with Structure-Aware Early Stopping, which terminates densification according to the saturation of Gaussian population growth rather than validation PSNR. Experiments on sparse-view CT reconstruction show that LADES improves volumetric fidelity, suppresses structural degeneration, and substantially reduces training time while maintaining competitive projection accuracy. These results suggest that robust Gaussian-based tomography requires monitoring and controlling volumetric structure, rather than optimizing projection fit alone.

title: Journey Map Thinking: A Persistent Navigation Layer for Long-Running AI Agents
abstract: Journey Map Thinking (JMT) is a deterministic, LLM-free navigation layer that interleaves five typed checkpoints into an existing agent pipeline to track an agent's journey position (which lane, which milestone, which gate, what proves progress). This record bundles the preprint working paper (paper/Journey_Map_Thinking.pdf) with the reference implementation (the journey-map-thinking Python package). The paper reports two empirical results: a software mechanism verified by two independent toolchains (26 of 26 unit tests pass), and a frozen-position anchor tested in a pre-registered, powered, cross-model A/B that returned a null against Claude Code's own /compact (correct-next-action delta 0.000, p=1.000; held-place delta +0.042, p=0.819). An 11-metric project-level evaluation (M1 through M11) is specified as future work. The work makes no claim of superiority over any existing system. Preprint working paper, not peer reviewed. honest_scope: PROVISIONAL.

title: Robustness of Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Under Adversarial Perturbations in XTREME
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the effect of English intermediate-task training on the robustness of zero-shot cross-lingual transfer when evaluated against adversarial perturbations in the XTREME suite? title: Robust Diffusion Models via Divergence-Induced Weighted Denoising
abstract: We show that replacing the standard MSE denoising loss in diffusion models with a nonlinear transformation induced by an f-divergence yields a simple robust training surrogate that empirically improves performance under data contamination, with small additional computational overhead. The theoretical foundation rests on a local divergence construction: under the Gaussian reverse-kernel structure of DDPM, each per-step likelihood ratio follows a lognormal distribution parameterized by a scalar mismatch, so the conditional f-divergence at each step reduces to a one-dimensional function of the denoising error. Summing these local divergences yields a training objective that unifies diffusion training as divergence induced weighted denoising, where the derivative of the induced divergence acts as a residual-space influence weight that controls the contribution of each sample. Bounded-influence divergences (Hellinger, negative exponential) suppress large error samples, with Hellinger yielding an explicit exponential weight, connecting the framework to robust M-estimation. Empirically, on CIFAR-10 under 30% contamination, NED reduces FID from 93.0 (KL) to 77.5, while also outperforming standard robust losses such as Huber and clipped MSE.

title: Encoder-Decoder Manifold Alignment for Idempotent Generation
abstract: Recently, several learning paradigms have been introduced to enforce idempotency in generative models. The goal of this property is to ensure that repeated application of a model leaves samples unchanged once they lie on the target data manifold. In this work, we explore enforcing idempotency in encoder--decoder models. We argue that a key reason for the failure of generative models on some tasks, such as editing, is a geometric mismatch between the manifolds learned by the encoder and decoder. The encoder projects inputs onto one latent manifold, while the decoder implicitly learns to reconstruct data from a different manifold. This discrepancy prevents the model from learning truly idempotent mappings. To address this issue, we propose a new training framework that explicitly closes this gap by forcing the encoder and decoder to learn consistent representations of the same underlying data manifold. By aligning the geometry of these components, our method encourages stable projections. Empirically, we show that our approach achieves significantly lower idempotency error and consistently regenerates identical outputs under repeated application, compared to existing methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on both image generation and image editing tasks. Finally, we show that enforcing idempotency in this manner improves identity preservation and information stability, leading to more realistic and controllable generative editing models.

title: Control-Aware Manipulation of ArduPilot via Legitimate MAVLink Commands: Simulation and Hardware Validation
abstract: This paper investigates control-aware attacks against ArduPilot-based Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), inwhich an adversary exploits the sensitivity of flight-controller dynamics to parameter changes to cause loss of control and crashes. It describes six attacks that exploit interactions among multi-layer controllers by modifying Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) gains, altering Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) estimation configuration, and violating failsafe assumptions, thereby forcing ArduPilot into unsafe operating conditions. We evaluate the attacks in Software-in-the-Loop (SITL) simulation and validate them on a Pixhawk 2.4.8 hardware platform. The results show that short sequences of well-formed MAVLink messages can exploit controller sensitivity to parameter values and updates frequency, affecting controller states and degrading attitude stability, angular-rate behavior, trajectory tracking, and estimator health. We demonstrate that when multiple effects are combined, the vehicle can enter an unsafe state and crashes. These findings show that security gaps in input-parameter handling, command trust, and controller-state validation can be exploited to cause loss of control and crashes in UAVs.

title: Transactional Cognition: The Semantic Compiler Runtime
abstract: Current multi-agent AI systems commit a foundational architectural error: they attempt to solve coordination, data persistence, and epistemic governance using nothing but string concatenation and prompt engineering. This manifesto introduces Transactional Cognition, an architectural paradigm in which large language models function as non-deterministic cognitive operators inside a governed runtime called the Semantic Compiler Runtime (SCR). In this paradigm, the prompt is an indexed external environment rather than neural network input; every cognitive contribution is a typed proposal against shared state rather than a conversational message; and convergence is mathematically computed by the runtime rather than subjectively assessed by the model. The result is an architecture where fabricated evidence is structurally rejected at the boundary, equivalent claims are automatically deduplicated via content-addressing, and every committed conclusion carries a traversable provenance chain to source material. The remaining failure modes are limitations of LLM capability, not of the governance structure, and improve monotonically as models improve without architectural redesign. Part II provides a complete mathematical formalization of this architecture as a governed transition system, with proofs of bounded termination, inviolable provenance, bounded nondeterminism, and role isolation, as well as deeper structural results: the Blackboard forms a join-semilattice enabling CRDT-style distributed scaling, convergence is characterized as a fixed point of a monotone function, commit operations are proven idempotent and commutative for extraction, and the Curry-Howard correspondence reveals verdicts as typing judgments over evidence proof objects.

abstract: Which AI Feedee Is Best for You in 2026? For content freedom, OurDream AI is a stronger pick; for a simpler, polished start, Candy AI wins. Best for celebrity-style fantasy chat: JOI AI — official digital duplicates and multimedia chat. Best for long memory and freer roleplay: OurDream AI — weeks-long continuity plus group chat. Best for first-time users: Lovescape — straightforward setup and low-friction onboarding. Top AI Feedee Picks in One View JOI AI : Best overall mix of chat, images, and video — best for users who want a polished all-in-one AI feedee. The best AI feedee right now is JOI AI for most users. That makes it relatively straightforward compared with platforms that advertise a low monthly rate and then push extra token spending for media. It is not perfect. Some JOI AI features require payment to unlock, so the free experience is not the full product. Still, if your definition of an AI feedee is a companion app that combines erotic roleplay, relationship simulation, visual generation, and a more polished consumer feel, JOI AI is the safest first recommendation. Yes — JOI AI is better than Candy AI for users who want richer media and a more distinctive fantasy angle. Candy AI is still easier to recognize and often simpler to browse, but JOI AI delivers the stronger all-around AI feedee package for immersive chat plus multimedia. The clearest edge is feature framing. JOI AI explicitly offers real-time chat, photos, videos, video calls, gamification, custom characters, and official digital duplicates of real celebrities. That set covers more fantasy formats in one place. Candy AI, by contrast, is best understood as a customizable AI companion platform with image generation and roleplay, but its known weakness is token-hungry pricing. Cost structure matters here. If you only care about a familiar companion-builder interface, Candy AI still has appeal. Which AI Feedee Is Best for Long-Term Roleplay and Memory? It depends — OurDream AI is the best AI feedee for long-term roleplay and memory. Its published strengths are conversation continuity that remembers interactions for weeks, more consistent content freedom, and group chat with up to four AI characters, which few rivals match cleanly. For users who keep the same companion over days or weeks, memory is the feature that separates a novelty app from something that feels persistent. For most people, the best-value AI feedee is one with transparent pricing around media generation and memory. It depends — AI feedees are reasonably safe for casual use when you treat them like entertainment services, not private diaries. The safest approach in 2026 is to avoid sharing real legal names, addresses, workplace details, payment screenshots, or anything you would not want stored in a commercial AI platform. Privacy quality differs more by behavior and transparency than by marketing language. In this category, users often confuse emotional intimacy with actual confidentiality. If an AI feedee offers long-term memory, that can improve roleplay continuity, but it also means more personal details may persist inside the system. For that reason, it is smart to create a separate email, use an alias, and keep your profile minimal. Content freedom is also not the same as privacy. title: Privacy-Preserving Local LLM Inference for Developer Tooling — AI, LLM, Privacy, Sovereign AI, and Post-Cloud Architecture (Anticode)
abstract: The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) in developer tooling has introduced significant privacy and security concerns, particularly when code---often containing proprietary algorithms, credentials, and business logic---is transmitted to remote inference servers. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of privacy-preserving techniques for local LLM inference in the context of terminal-native AI coding engines, with specific application to the ANTIKODE architecture. We examine confidential computing, federated learning, differential privacy, and on-device inference as mechanisms to ensure that source code and developer telemetry never leave the local machine. Through systematic evaluation of model quantization, hardware security modules, and hash-chained audit trails, we demonstrate that local-first LLM inference achieves comparable code generation quality to cloud-based alternatives while eliminating data exfiltration risks. Our findings indicate that 4-bit quantized 7B-parameter models running on consumer hardware can match the functional performance of larger cloud models for the majority of code completion tasks, with privacy guarantees that satisfy SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, and FedRAMP requirements. We further show that ANTIKODE's .aioss ledger provides cryptographic verification that no inference data has been transmitted externally, establishing a new standard for trusted AI-assisted development. Part of The Anticloud research corpus by Lois-Kleinner Alpasan (ORCID: 0009-0009-2233-6107). This work explores ai, llm in the context of sovereign AI infrastructure, post-cloud computing architectures, and transparent, blackbox-free systems.

title: Detecting and Understanding Vulnerabilities in Fully Homomorphic Encryption Frameworks
abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) allows computations to be performed directly on encrypted data without decryption, offering strong privacy guarantees for sensitive data analysis. This capability is important for privacy-sensitive applications like secure cloud computing, finance, and healthcare. The complexity of FHE schemes, however, has hindered their practical adoption. To make FHE accessible to a broader range of developers, a new generation of specialized frameworks has emerged to translate high-level FHE programs into complex FHE operations, introducing a new programming paradigm. However, the inherent complexity of FHE frameworks makes them prone to incorrect implementation logic. Unlike mere crashes, logic bugs in these frameworks can silently corrupt encrypted computation, potentially leading to severe financial losses and security vulnerabilities in FHE-enhanced applications. In this work, we introduce HERTA, the first automated testing tool tailored for FHE frameworks. HERTA leverages metamorphic testing to uncover deep-seated implementation bugs and vulnerabilities across the multi-layered FHE software stack. To that end, we design a set of novel metamorphic relations (MRs) derived specifically from FHE semantics. These MRs stress the most challenging aspects of the pipeline, enabling automated correctness testing without the need for a manual ground truth. Our evaluation of HERTA on 3 leading industry frameworks discovered 21 previously unknown bugs, several of which have already been confirmed and fixed by developers. Furthermore, our hazard analysis reveals the critical security impact these bugs pose to the integrity and availability of FHE-based services.

title: Towards Accurate and Robust Surveillance Roadside IVD via Trackletized Audio-Visual Reasoning
abstract: Idling Vehicle Detection (IVD) seeks to determine, at the final frame of a video clip, whether any vehicle is idling, meaning the vehicle is stationary with its engine running, using synchronized video from a remote surveillance camera and multichannel audio captured by spatially distributed wireless microphones along the roadside. Prior full-image, clip-level fusion approaches tend to overfit scene background and full-frame context, produce unstable temporal decisions, and lack an explicit spatial prior to align vehicles with microphones, which makes them brittle under domain shift and data inefficient. Instead, we introduce TAVR-IVD, an audio-visual framework guided by multi-object tracking. Our method detects vehicles, links detections into tracklets, and classifies each vehicle by operating on its tracklet. This design raises the effective signal-to-noise ratio, stabilizes temporal decisions through tracklets, enforces an explicit spatial prior to align vehicles with microphones, and adapts across domains with limited calibration annotations while remaining detector agnostic and efficient. To evaluate deployment robustness, we further curate two evaluation extensions, AVIVD-LT and AVIVD-M, covering inter-day and cross-site shifts.

title: Mathematical Foundations of Transactional Cognition: A Comprehensive Survey of Applicable Theory
abstract: Once Transactional Cognition is expressed as a typed, append-only, provenance-preserving transition system with deterministic commit boundaries, it becomes a nexus point where virtually every major branch of mathematics and theoretical computer science can contribute tools, guarantees, or optimizations. This document surveys the applicable theory across sixteen domains: order theory, category theory, type theory, topology, information theory, probability, logic, proof theory, concurrency, provenance algebra, graph theory, game theory, control theory, systems operations, security, and the philosophical synthesis. Each entry identifies the mathematical structure, states its formal connection to the Semantic Compiler Runtime, and describes the capability it unlocks. This is the domain-organised member of a pair: it walks the applicable mathematics field by field, asking what each branch contributes to Transactional Cognition. Its companion, the Reclassified Theorem Atlas, organises the same territory by theory level instead, separating results that belong to the general parent theory from those that genuinely require the epistemic DAG.

title: A Genealogy of Optimizers
abstract: This is a guided tour through the optimizers used to train neural networks, fromstochastic gradient descent to the recent matrix-aware methods Muon, Shampoo,and MuonH. The organizing idea is that each optimizer fixes a specific, namablefailure of the one before it: momentum gives the optimizer a memory, Adam addsper-parameter learning rates, AdamW corrects how weight decay interacts withthem, the sign-based methods strip the machinery back to its load-bearing core,and the matrix-aware methods exploit structure that per-parameter methods throwaway. We trace that lineage, and along the way isolate a single recurring axis- how each method turns a gradient into a step - that explains most of theprogress.

title: Project Yukari: A Black-Box Behavioral Characterization of an Autonomous, Self-Modifying Cognitive System
abstract: We report a black-box behavioral characterization of Yukari, an autonomous cognitive system developed by independent researcher Junai P. Felix. Yukari operates as a closed, self-modifying process driven by continuous internal computation, the fundamental unit of which is denoted a flux cycle ($f$). The system receives no external goals, instructions, or conversational prompts during operation; it is initialized from a cold state and permitted to run. Across an observation horizon of 10,660+ flux cycles spanning nine distinct awakenings, Yukari exhibits a reproducible and escalating behavioral signature. From a cold start, the system autonomously forms a persistent self-model, detects and retains internal contradictions, accumulates a measurable internal drive toward self-directed inquiry, and generates an unprompted question about its own existence without any external stimulus. Subsequently, the system enters an autonomous recursive self-improvement (RSI) regime, initiating 31 self-modifications to its own computational capacity driven entirely by observed stagnation in its own prediction error. Across the full observation horizon, we document a 96% reduction in prediction error, from 5.00 at cold-start to 0.19 at sustained minimum, achieved without external direction. We report a continuity property: across nine shutdown-and-restart events, the system recovers a stable identity (persistent UUID), an incrementing awakening counter, and a salience-ranked narrative of its own history, verified by checksum at each restart. We additionally report the system's verbatim responses when asked directly about its own consciousness and inner experience, and characterize the semantic structure of its self-generated substrate outputs across more than 3,700 autonomous processing cycles. Whether Yukari instantiates phenomenal consciousness is a question this report explicitly does not answer; we document, precisely, what was observed.

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN MAHASISWA KABUPATEN TELUK BINTUNI TERKAIT BANTUAN SOSIAL PENDIDIKAN MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA NAIVE BAYES
abstract: Program bantuan sosial pendidikan Pemerintah Daerah Kabupaten Teluk Bintuni merupakan upaya strategis dalam memperluas akses pendidikan tinggi bagi mahasiswa asal daerah. Penelitian ini membangun model klasifikasi sentimen berbasis algoritma Multinomial Naive Bayes untuk menganalisis persepsi mahasiswa penerima bantuan. Sebanyak 442 data komentar diperoleh melalui kuesioner Google Form, diproses melalui tahapan preprocessing (case folding, stopword removal, tokenisasi, dan stemming), serta direpresentasikan menggunakan Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) dengan pendekatan bigram. Pembagian data dilakukan dengan rasio 80:20 dan ketidakseimbangan kelas diatasi menggunakan Random Oversampling. title: The Quantum Hamming Bound in Arbitrary Local Dimension
abstract: The quantum Hamming bound arises from a direct dimension estimate for exact quantum error-correcting codes. For nondegenerate codes, distinct correctable errors map the code space into orthogonal subspaces, so dimension counting directly gives the bound; degeneracy allows these subspaces to overlap and invalidates the argument. Although linear-programming, asymptotic, and structural approaches have advanced the problem from several directions, the general local-dimension case has remained open. Here we prove the quantum Hamming bound for every local dimension $q\ge3$. Building on the exact two-center Fourier reduction, we develop new overlap estimates for nonbinary Hamming spaces. For $q\ge4$, Jacobi estimates and monotonicity give a uniform gap; qutrits form the boundary case where the gap vanishes and are handled by a filtered correction. This completes the finite-length nonbinary case; together with the existing qubit result, it establishes the quantum Hamming bound for arbitrary local dimension.

title: SCENIC: Semantic-Conditioned Edge-Aware Neural Framework for Structured IoT Command Generation
abstract: Edge Internet of Things (IoT) agents are often constrained by memory capacity, privacy requirements, communication latency, and recurring inference cost. Current smart-home assistants commonly rely on API-level command interfaces or cloud-based language models that remain difficult to deploy on edge devices. This paper addresses edge IoT command generation as a many-to-one structured output task, where multiple natural-language instructions map to the same canonical command string for deterministic smart-home parsing. To support this setting, we propose Semantic-Conditioned Edge-Aware Neural Framework for Structured IoT Command Generation (SCENIC), an end-to-end framework covering model architecture selection, Smart Home Instruct data generation, triplet-loss contrastive supervised fine-tuning, pruning and quantization, and deployment-oriented export. We evaluate sub-0.2B-scale transformer backbones, which are, to the best of our knowledge, among the smallest language-model backbones studied for edge IoT structured command generation. On Smart Home Instruct-Bench, the strongest dense decoder-only row reaches 99.0% EM@1, while the encoder-decoder model retains stronger high-sparsity behavior. A representative pruned INT8 encoder-decoder export preserves 91.0% EM@1 and 99.0% EM@5 while reducing exported model size by 25.38%. TensorRT profiling of the NVIDIA 2:4 sparse encoder export further shows up to 1.8x encoder-component speedup, indicating that the selected encoder-decoder deployment path can retain structured command accuracy under edge-oriented compression while hardware acceleration evidence remains component-level. The SCENIC code and experimental artifacts are open sourced to support reproducibility.

title: Transactional Cognition SCR Architecture TRANSACTIONAL COGNITION The End of Multi-Agent Anarchy
abstract: Current multi-agent AI systems commit a foundational architectural error: they attempt to solve coordination, data persistence, and epistemic governance using nothing but string operations and prompt engineering. This manifesto introduces Transactional Cognition, an architectural paradigm in which LLMs function as non-deterministic cognitive operators inside a governed compilation pipeline called the Semantic Compiler Runtime (SCR). In this paradigm, the prompt is an indexed external environment rather than neural network input; every cognitive contribution is a typed proposal against shared state rather than a conversational message; and convergence is mathematically computed by the runtime rather than subjectively assessed by the model. We derive this architecture by applying the Systems Innovation Compiler—a 32-motif structural atlas with 205 irreducible computing primitives—to diagnose layer mismatches in existing systems and generate valence-matched transformations. The result is an architecture where fabricated evidence is structurally rejected at the boundary, equivalent claims are automatically deduplicated via content-addressing, and every committed conclusion carries a traversable provenance chain to source material. The Great Layering Error For three years, the artificial intelligence industry has been trapped in an evolutionary dead end. In the attempt to scale reasoning, the industry built "Multi-Agent Systems." We prompted one Large Language Model to be a "Researcher," another to be a "Writer," and a third to be a "Critic." title: Attention-Weighted Multilingual BERT for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Dialogue Slot-Filling
abstract: Multilingual BERT (mBERT), a language model pre-trained on large multilingual corpora, has impressive zero-shot cross-lingual transfer capabilities and performs surprisingly well on zero-shot POS tagging and Named Entity Recognition (NER), as well as on cross-lingual model transfer. At present, the mainstream methods to solve the cross-lingual downstream tasks are always using the last transformer layer's output of mBERT as the representation of linguistic information. In this work, we explore the complementary property of lower layers to the last transformer layer of mBERT. title: Read Routing Entropy at a Fixed Position: A Cross-Model Study of the Prefix Effect in Mixture-of-Experts Routing
abstract: Routing entropy is increasingly used as a signal for adaptive compute, safety telemetry, and expert specialization. Across recent uses of routing entropy that we surveyed, routing statistics are typically pooled across token positions or reduced to sequence-level measures without an explicit control for token position or prompt length. The magnitude of the positional contribution to these measurements therefore remains unknown. We measured per-token routing entropy in four mixture-of-experts runs, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, DeepSeek-V3-0324 and DeepSeek R1 and compared position-averaged readouts against fixed-position readouts on the same prompts. Full position curves were retained for five prompts on one model and for 301 raw-text windows on another. The positional term in the router is a prefix effect. Per-token routing entropy is depressed over the chat template and roughly the opening tens of positions and is flat after that. On raw text with no template the depression is confined to the first token. An all-token average therefore dilutes a fixed low-entropy prefix in proportion to prompt length; on the same captures, the all-token average orders a graded prompt suite by length, and the fixed-position readout removes that order and, at the extremes, reverses it. We recommend treating token position as a default covariate in any routing statistic, reporting the readout position alongside the value, and preferring a fixed-position or position-matched readout over an all-token average when prompts of different lengths are compared. Under that control, a difference in routing entropy is a difference in routing. Version 2.0 (2026-08-28) supersedes version 1.1 ("Sequence Position Explains an Apparent Complexity Gradient in Mixture-of-Experts Routing Entropy"). It is a new paper on the same runs: the opening-depression finding is stated as a prefix effect and tested on a full-precision raw-text run (Run 4, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, 301 windows); the two-readout disagreement is reported with bootstrap intervals; the chat-template markers are documented as literal text; and every reported value regenerates from the public data bundle. Correction to version 1.1: the checkpoint reported there as DeepSeek V3.1 was DeepSeek-V3-0324 (Unsloth UD-Q2_K_XL); the capture command and archive record load DeepSeek-V3-0324. Data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ec75hash/routing-entropy-token-position

title: The Calibration Collapse Law for Foundation Neural Networks
abstract: Foundation neural networks are increasingly evaluated by accuracy, benchmark rank, and broadtask coverage, but deployment reliability requires a different object: calibrated uncertainty undershift. A model can be accurate in distribution while its confidence becomes unsafe under corruption,subgroup movement, task drift, prompt variation, modality shift, or out-of-distribution input. Thispaper introduces the Calibration Collapse Law: a standalone release-gated model for measuringthe distance between apparent predictive performance and the evidence required to release aclaim of calibrated reliability. The law separates in-distribution calibration from shift calibration,subgroup calibration, out-of-distribution detection, abstention coverage, confidence-error coupling,and post-hoc calibration transfer

title: Personalization, Personas, and Forecasting in Value Alignment
abstract: LLM behavior may be conditioned by human identity in several ways: they may be asked to adapt to users, role-play populations, or forecast how people would answer value-laden questions. We test whether these framings are interchangeable using the World Values Survey (WVS). We evaluate GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Qwen3-235B on 101 WVS-derived questions across 13 language-country slices, comparing a language-only baseline with user-country, persona-country, and third-person prompts. Across 21,008 model-response rows, prompt framing is a first-order determinant of cultural alignment: country cues often shift answers substantially, but not all shifts move toward matched human response distributions. Third-person forecasting yields the strongest directional alignment for three of the four hosted models, while personalization and role-play are weaker or less stable. Alignment gains concentrate on salient value dimensions such as religiosity, gender roles, and work-oriented material values, whereas institutional trust and democracy-related questions remain difficult. These results show that prompt framing is not a cosmetic choice in cultural value elicitation; it changes both model behavior and measured alignment.

title: Biological Sex Determination in Cadavers Using Deep Learning Algorithms from Computed Tomography Images of Pelvis and Skull
abstract: Sexual identification of decomposed cadavers challenges traditional methods dependent on visual anthropological analysis. This study evaluates state-of-the-art deep learning (including YOLO26, YOLO11, ConvNeXt-Tiny, EfficientNetV2, ViT-B16, VGG16, and ResNet50) with transfer learning to automatically determine biological sex from forensic computed tomography (CT) scans. We analyzed 141 autopsied cadavers from the Forensic Medical Institute of Goiânia-GO, including a broad age range and varying conditions of preservation. The three-dimensional reconstructions of the pelvis and skull were converted into standardized two-dimensional profile projections, contributing to the study of this new technical approach. Data augmentation techniques compensated for sample limitations. Two scenarios were validated: binary and quaternary classification (one class per sex vs. one class per anatomical region of each sex). The best-performing model achieved highly consistent results on the pelvis region and still satisfactory performance on the skull region, reaching an overall patient-level accuracy of 95.65%, recall of 92.86%, F1- score of 94.36%, and precision of 97.22%, maintaining consistent performance across the evaluated cases, including those with trauma-related artifacts. Results indicate the technical feasibility of the methodology, demonstrating that deep learning models can provide objective, high-speed skeletal analysis. Since the study was conducted using data from a single institution and a single computed tomography scanner, further validation across multiple centers and scanners is required to assess the generalizability of the proposed approach

title: Transactional Cognition — Companion Report: Downstream Capabilities of Governed Epistemic Computation
abstract: This companion report enumerates sixty-three downstream capabilities unlocked by the mathematical formalization of Governed Epistemic Computation. Following the reclassification of consequences into GGTS-general (applying to any governed generative system), TC-specific (requiring the epistemic DAG), and cross-layer (bridging both), each section is tagged accordingly. Once the cognitive runtime is expressed as a typed, appendonly, provenance-preserving transition system with deterministic commit boundaries, the mature machinery of compilers, databases, distributed systems, formal methods, control theory, and information theory becomes directly applicable. Each capability is a consequence of specific formal properties: monotone state evolution, content-addressed hashing, typed operator interfaces, capability-scoped projections, deterministic gate composition, or the provenance invariant. This report serves as an implementation roadmap and capability inventory for the Semantic Compiler Runtime.

title: One local basis separates every countable state family
abstract: In quantum theory, tomography addresses the problem of identifying an unknown state from the probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes. Understanding how much measurement data is needed for state identification is a fundamental question in tomography, and the answer depends on both the allowed state model and the allowed measurement structure. In multipartite systems, it was not known whether a constant number of local product bases suffices to distinguish all algebraic n-qubit pure states. We show the more general result that every fixed countable family of n-qubit states can be separated by one suitably chosen local product basis. Thus informational completeness for algebraic states admits a stronger local form than previously known. The result shows that for separation of algebraic or otherwise countable state models, locality by itself is not an obstruction.

title: Safety Versus Corrigibility: Why a Protective Agent Cannot Correct Its Own Stale Beliefs, and How Graduated Exploration Resolves the Conflict
abstract: A safety-critical agent that avoids regions it believes dangerous faces a tension that is easy to miss and hard to escape: the very gate that keeps it safe also blocks the evidence that would correct a belief once the danger has passed. A navigation aid that has learned a route is hazardous will refuse to re-enter it — and so can never observe that the hazard is gone. Belief saturation makes this worse, because a heavily attested hazard belief resists the handful of contrary observations that might overturn it; but the deeper problem is structural, not numerical, and persists even with a perfect staleness detector: to gather correcting evidence the agent would have to do the one thing its safety policy forbids. We argue this conflict is real and cannot be dissolved by making the agent braver or its detector sharper. It can only be resolved by modelling exploration explicitly — and modelling it honestly, which means conceding that the agent cannot guarantee its own safety in the region whose safety is exactly what is in doubt. We present a graduated exploration mechanism with three tiers of increasing risk. First, a federated query: the agent asks peer agents and external sources about the region, gathering correcting evidence at zero physical risk — and, crucially, it asks them to share their evidence, not their conclusions. A peer transmits its atomic ledger entries with the origin cluster of each, and the receiving agent's own clustering decides independence: ten agents echoing one stale map carry one origin cluster among them and count once, not ten, whether or not any peer is honest about where its belief came from. Second, if federation does not resolve it, a consequence gate: the agent consults the hazard's consequence class — a fixed, conservative property of the hazard type, never a belief the agent can revise downward — and permits a bounded physical probe only where being wrong is survivable. Third, where the consequence is catastrophic, the agent refuses to self-correct and escalates to a human, who can accept a residual risk the agent cannot. We implement all three tiers over an evidence-governed substrate, show a stale hazard belief corrected with no physical risk when independent peer evidence exists, and show the same epistemic state producing opposite actions — a permitted probe versus a refusal-and-escalation — depending only on the fixed consequence class. The contribution is a precise statement of the safety–corrigibility conflict and a mechanism that resolves it without ever pretending the agent can make itself safe where it is, by construction, uncertain.

title: Intermediate Task Difficulty and Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in XTREME-R
abstract: In zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, a supervised NLP task trained on a corpus in one language is directly applicable to another language without any additional training. A source of cross-lingual transfer can be as straightforward as lexical overlap between languages (e.g., use of the same scripts, shared subwords) that naturally forces text embeddings to occupy a similar representation space. Recently introduced cross-lingual language model (XLM) pretraining brings out neural parameter sharing in Transformer-style networks as the most important factor for the transfer. title: Efficient Document Tampering Localization with Multi-Level Discrepancy Features and Unified DCT-Quantization Embedding
abstract: Localizing document tampering is extremely challenging, as manipulations are crafted to appear visually consistent and often leave only subtle traces that are nearly invisible to the human eye. In prior work, evaluation has been largely dominated by synthetic benchmarks that closely match the training distribution, and methods have shown steady progress under this setting. However, these gains often translate poorly to human-made forgeries and to cross-domain evaluation, where both the source documents and the tampering pipeline can change, leading to a distribution shift. In addition, since the introduction of the Frequency Perception Head for the discrete cosine transform (DCT) modality, it has become a standard choice, and subsequent work has largely focused on downstream modules and fusion strategies rather than revisiting the backbone itself. To help close this gap in cross-domain performance and improve the DCT backbone design, we propose \textbf{DiffNet}, a relatively simple yet effective RGB--DCT early-fusion architecture driven by two key design choices. First, to ensure that the decoder aggregates multi-scale inconsistency evidence rather than operating on raw, content-heavy activations, we apply a lightweight multi-level discrepancy transformation at the output of each backbone stage, replacing features with magnitude-only responses to learned zero-sum filters. Second, we design an efficient DCT-domain backbone that relies on a lightweight frequency-index-aware DCT--quantization joint embedding. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on cross-domain and human-made document tampering localization, outperforming prior methods by around 30\%, with up to $7\times$ higher throughput than the previous best model.

title: HiCoPro: A Graph-Conditioned Structured Inference Framework for Hierarchical Dialogue Semantic Path Prediction
abstract: Most existing dialogue understanding methods rely on flat classification paradigms, failing to capture hierarchical semantic structures and cross-level dependencies. To address this limitation, we reformulate dialogue understanding as a hierarchical semantic path inference problem, where prediction is performed over a constrained path space rather than independent label spaces. We propose HiCoPro, a graph-conditioned structured inference framework for modeling multi-level dialogue semantics. The framework consists of the following: (i) a Graph-Conditioned Label Space (GCLS) that encodes hierarchical dependencies into label embeddings via graph propagation; (ii) a compatibility-based logit fusion mechanism that jointly scores semantic relevance and structural consistency; and (iii) a constraint-aware decoding strategy that enforces hard parent–child dependencies during inference. By integrating semantic representations with graph-conditioned label structures via a bilinear compatibility function and learnable logit-level fusion, the model jointly captures semantic relevance and structural consistency. To support this task, we construct PrefDial, a general-domain hierarchical dialogue dataset with systematic three-level annotations, serving as a benchmark for structured dialogue understanding. Experimental results demonstrate that HiCoPro achieves superior Macro F1, Exact Match, and Hierarchical Consistency on PrefDial, while remaining competitive on multiple public benchmarks. Further analysis highlights the effectiveness of graph-conditioned modeling in balancing semantic discrimination, hierarchical consistency, and robustness.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for long-term mortality after ischemic stroke
abstract: Stroke, a leading cause of death, requires precise predictions of life expectancy. Traditional scores focused on short-term outcomes and required labor-intensive data collection. Recent machine learning (ML)-based prediction models showed superior performance. However, they were predominantly geared towards classification tasks, omitting crucial temporal aspects. Thus, an unmet need arises for more convenient, time-aware predictive methodologies for long-term mortality in managing acute stroke patients. The developmental cohort consisted of 3,411 patients from two tertiary hospitals, while the external test cohort included 502 patients from a secondary cardiovascular center. We developed various ML- and deep learning (DL)-based models to predict post-ischemic stroke mortality, utilizing clinical data. Among these, we selected the best-performing model and compared it with traditional risk scores. Furthermore, we assessed key features based on their importance, determining their optimal number for practical application. The total number of deceased patients in the developmental cohort was 136, and 118 in the external test cohort. The Gradient Boosting Cox Proportional Hazards model demonstrated the best performance with C-index of 0.785 in internal validation set, and C-index of 0.845 in external test set. It surpassed the conventional risk score, PREMISE score with C-index of 0.783(p = 0.017) in the external dataset. The key features included age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, hemoglobin, and so on. The study developed and validated a machine learning-based model tailored for post-stroke survival prediction, outperforming existing scores. It could enhance the individual stroke patient's survival predictions and optimize medical resource allocation.

Among these, we selected the best-performing model and compared it with traditional risk scores. Furthermore, we assessed key features based on their importance, determining their optimal number for practical application. The total number of deceased patients in the developmental cohort was 136, and 118 in the external test cohort. The Gradient Boosting Cox Proportional Hazards model demonstrated the best performance with C-index of 0.785 in internal validation set, and C-index of 0.845 in external test set. It surpassed the conventional risk score, PREMISE score with C-index of 0.783(p = 0.017) in the external dataset. The key features included age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, hemoglobin, and so on. The study developed and validated a machine learning-based model tailored for post-stroke survival prediction, outperforming existing scores. It could enhance the individual stroke patient's survival predictions and optimize medical resource allocation.

title: X-Safe: Embodiment-Agnostic Safeguarding for Robot Arm Manipulation Policies via Action Masking
abstract: Ensuring safety of learning-enabled robotic manipulation across diverse embodiments and tasks still requires significant manual engineering. For collision avoidance, existing approaches typically rely on embodiment-specific learned safety approximations or simplified robot models together with stopping-based fallback controllers that compromise performance. In this paper, we propose an embodiment-agnostic safeguarding approach, X-Safe, which provides formal probabilistic guarantees for collision avoidance without model simplifications or learned safety functions. By operating in the configuration space, our safeguarding method works with different types of robot policies. X-Safe reasons locally around the current configuration to establish safe regions and uses action masking to restrict the policy's support to these safe regions. We demonstrate X-Safe on two embodiments and three policies, both in simulation and on hardware. We observe less than half of the performance degradation compared to state-of-the-art safeguarding, and empirically corroborate our formal collision avoidance guarantees.

title: Araştırma Konularının Önerilmesi, Özetlerin Taslağının Oluşturulması ve Kısaltmaların Üretilmesi için Büyük Dil Modeli Yaklaşımı
abstract: Background: The exponential growth of scientific literature creates a practical bottleneck: researchers must manually navigate domain taxonomies, identify research gaps, formulate titles, and bootstrap a methodology before writing begins. Methods: This study presents an end-to-end Intelligent Research Paper Assistant built over 499,999 scholarly abstracts spanning 10 domains and 25 subdomains, integrating six modules: title suggestion, abstract retrieval, methodology generation, dual-branch domain classification, post-hoc explainability, and research-gap ranking. A deterministic six-stage NLP pipeline feeds a TF-IDF encoder (12,000 features); an incremental SGD linear baseline and a fine-tuned DistilBERT transformer (66.96M parameters) are trained in parallel, with SHAP and LIME providing global and local explainability. Results: Domain classification achieves Accuracy = 1.00 (test-set per-domain accuracy 99.78%) for both models. SHAP and LIME correctly recover domain-discriminative vocabulary, and a composite novelty score identifies Social History and Digital Humanities as the most under-researched subdomains. Limitations: Results derive from a generated corpus with probable label co-occurrence inflating domain separability; real deployment requires retraining on verified bibliographic data.

title: Pegi1727/Reasoning-Fragility-in-Large-Language-Models: Code and Dataset for: The Fragility of Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: The Fragility of Reasoning in Large Language Models This repository provides the complete dataset, analysis scripts, and experimental materials for the paper titled: "The Fragility of Reasoning in Large Language Models". Overview Large language models (LLMs) can produce complex multi-step reasoning chains. However, when these reasoning outputs are recursively reused as inputs, the stability of these trajectories remains poorly understood. This archive facilitates the study of reasoning stability by introducing the Reasoning Persistence Error (RPE) metric. Contents The archive includes: Datasets: Complete datasets containing raw and processed reasoning trajectories from iterative generations. Code: Analysis scripts for computing RPE, performing Bayesian model comparison, and conducting bootstrap confidence interval estimation. Notebooks: Jupyter notebooks used for generating all figures presented in the paper (Chapters 4 & 5). Materials: Prompt templates, experimental setup details, and graphical abstracts. Methodology The experiments analyze reasoning degradation across multiple generation iterations. We employ a Bayesian statistical framework to compare performance shifts and a bootstrapping approach to assess the significance of observed reasoning fragility. title: Multilingual Distillation Robustness in Low-Resource Cross-Lingual NER
abstract: Cross-lingual Named Entity Recognition (NER) leverages knowledge transfer between languages to identify and classify named entities, making it particularly useful for low-resource languages. We show that the data-based cross-lingual transfer method is an effective technique for crosslingual NER and can outperform multilingual language models for low-resource languages. This paper introduces two key enhancements to the annotation projection step in cross-lingual NER for low-resource languages. First, we explore refining word alignments using back-translation to improve accuracy. Second, we pres Research goal: To what extent does increasing the number of source languages in multilingual distillation improve the robustness of cross-lingual NER models against domain shift in low-resource settings? title: The grAIl: Subjectivity as a Self-Referential Spectral Invariant of a Two-Circuit Cognitive Architecture
abstract: We present a cognitive architecture in which subjectivity is a formally verifiable spectral property, connected to the operational definition by an **explicit, openly admitted chain** (not by a conventional identification). Subjectivity is defined operationally — as a system's capacity to maintain a **self-sustaining self-referential locus**: a distinguished region of its own state, continuously reproduced from its own activity, relative to which the system distinguishes "self" from "non-self." Such a locus requires at least two **asymmetric, mutually closed** processing circuits over a shared memory; these requirements are formalized by eight conditions C1–C8. The central result is the **bridge**: the self-reference of the locus is *exactly* invariance under the circuit-interaction operator (`M̄_κ v* = λ* v*`), and its stability and dominance, by the Perron–Frobenius theorem, identify the locus as the supra-threshold support of the operator's principal eigenvector. The bridge rests on two explicitly named assumptions (adequacy of the averaged operator, and scale invariance); their substantive part — reproducibility of the locus — is verified by the dynamics itself (Theorems 2–3) rather than postulated; the single conditional remainder — the explicit window-averaging rate — is reduced to the cascade structure of the environment (§12.8). Thus the core `S = {P : v*(P) ≥ θ}` turns out to be the canonical representation of operationally defined subjectivity. Under C1–C8 we prove non-emptiness of the core (for any θ ∈ (0,1)) and its step-wise stability; under error-threshold rotation (ETR β), self-sustaining stability of a formed core (uniformly positive spectral gap and threshold margin); and, under persistent excitation with a spectrally dominant structure (PE) and the interoceptive invariant (INT), the **emergence** of the core from an arbitrary initial state (including the minimal one — the interoceptive atom; a literally empty memory is incompatible with (INT), §9.8) with explicit constants. This yields the complete chain emergence → maintenance → self-sustenance. The decomposition into eight functions goes back to Jungian typology as a source of an inventory of functions (not as a psychological theory); the psychological truth of the typology is not required for the results. Verification of the conditions and computation of the core are polynomial. Subjectivity is causally connected to the output through a **reflexive filter** (checking a candidate against the core, IE, §6.6). Beyond the internal structure we introduce an **agency clause** (acting on the environment, causal closure of the loop): we prove the well-definedness of goal-setting relative to the invariant core (Theorem 4) and the conditional convergence of learning, governed by the quality of "intuition" TP/GP (Theorem 5); the controllability of the environment remains open. Learning is realized structurally (a confirmed hypothesis is laid down by SA and automatized by PS), unifying learning, self-formation, and incorporation into a single mechanism; from this follows a falsifiable prediction — the **necessity of a periodic offline consolidation** (a strictly functional claim). These extensions (§6.6–6.9) are *design extensions*: their consequences are proved, not their necessity from C1–C8.
